title.en: Capital and Required Revenue by Completion Cohort (Table 6) with Revenue-Requirement Parameters
title.zh: 按建成年份的资本与所需收入（表 6）及收入要求参数

description.en: Appendix D, Table 6: for each 2025-2032 completion cohort, capacity (GW), initial cost Q_t, capital base at commissioning B_t = phi * Q_t, required mature annual operating cash flow, and required mature annual revenue, at a 10% required unlevered return and a 50% operating cash-flow margin. Parameters include the construction capital markup phi = 1.04527, capital-recovery factors a(10%,6) = 22.96% and a(10%,20) = 11.75%, the weighted annual capital charge of 19.37%, the IT (68%, 6-year life) vs non-IT (32%, 20-year life) split, and the footnote-11 reconciliation of the $8.973 trillion (Table 5) and $8.762 trillion (Table 6) investment figures.
description.zh: 附录 D 表 6：按 2025–2032 各建成年份 cohort 的容量（GW）、初始成本 Q_t、建成时点资本基座 B_t = φ × Q_t、所需成熟期年经营现金流与所需成熟期年收入（10% 无杠杆要求回报率、50% 经营现金流利润率）。参数包括建设期资本加成 φ = 1.04527、资本回收系数 a(10%,6) = 22.96% 与 a(10%,20) = 11.75%、加权年资本费用 19.37%、IT（占 68%、寿命 6 年）与非 IT（占 32%、寿命 20 年）拆分，以及脚注 11 对表 5 的 $8.973 万亿与表 6 的 $8.762 万亿投资额的差额调和。

notes: Table 6 note: 'Figures may not sum exactly because of rounding.'

Appendix D text values accompanying the table: initial cost approximately $8.762 trillion; capital base at commissioning approximately $9.159 trillion; required annual operating cash flow $1.774 trillion; mature annual revenue approximately $3.549 trillion by 2032; 8.8% of 2032 GDP of $40.481 trillion (PDF p.30).

Section V restatement: 'Under the central assumptions in Appendix D, the 2025-2032 buildout requires approximately $3.55 trillion in mature annual revenue to earn a 10% unlevered return at a 50% operating cash-flow margin' (PDF p.14).

The revenue calculation uses the capacity outcomes of Table 4, excludes capacity operational before 2025, retains reported completion years, and includes only capacity completed in 2025-32 (PDF p.29).

The exercise 'is not a forecast of AI revenues. Rather, it calculates the mature annual revenue required to recover the investment, replace depreciating capital, and compensate investors for the opportunity cost of capital' (PDF p.28).
Column mapping from raw: cost_bn_usd→cost_bn, capital_bn_usd→capital_bn, req_cf_bn_usd→req_cf_bn, req_rev_bn_usd→req_rev_bn; values verbatim.

provenance.quote_en: Table 6. Capital and Required Revenue by Completion Cohort
The 188.3 GW of capacity completed between 2025 and 2032 has an initial cost of approximately $8.762
Including the return on capital committed during construction raises the capital base at commissioning to approximately $9.159 trillion.
At a 10 percent required unlevered return, this capacity must generate $1.774 trillion in annual operating cash flow once all cohorts are operational and mature.
At a 50 percent operating cash-flow margin, this corresponds to mature annual revenue of approximately $3.549 trillion by 2032.
This represents 8.8% of 2032 GDP of $40.481 trillion.

At an 𝑟= 10% required unlevered return, the six-year and 20-year capital-recovery factors are 22.96% and 11.75%, respectively. The weighted annual capital charge is therefore 19.37% of the capital base.
We assume in Table 2 that IT equipment accounts for 68 percent of total cost. Based on current industry assessment and accounting practices, we assume IT has a six-year economic life.
Buildings, power infrastructure, cooling equipment, and other non-IT assets account for the remaining 32 percent and have a 20-year economic life.
At a 10 percent required return and a 𝜇= 50% margin, mature annual revenue equals 38.74% of the capital base.
The difference with the $8.973 trillion estimate in Table 5 is the $565 billion in costs incurred during 2025-2032 for data centers that will be operational after 2032
minus the $354 billion in costs that were incurred prior to 2025 on data centers completed in 2025–2032.
$41 million per MW in 2025 and 4 percent annual cost growth
the 54.0 GW of undated capacity assumed to be completed by 2032 is allocated equally across 2028–2032.
Under the central assumptions in Appendix D, the 2025–2032 buildout requires approximately $3.55 trillion in mature annual revenue to earn a 10% unlevered return at a 50% operating cash-flow margin.
